title: adaptive-response_format-handshake-metadata-and-human-readable-errors-for-tool-calls
author: Amira Patel
description: Context: Users and downstream adapters (OpenAI-compatible SDKs and function-call bridges) have been tripping over rigid schema enforcement when responses arrive incrementally or when tool-calls interleave with the model stream. This PR introduces a small, opt-in runtime handshake and a human-friendly error surface to reduce developer friction while preserving strict validation when customers opt in. Summary of changes: Introduces a lightweight response_format metadata handshake that is exchanged at stream start and allows the runtime to advertise support for: 1) schema versions (json-schema-v3), 2) adaptive_strictness levels (per-request hint: permissive|warn|strict), 3) snapshot markers for resumable streams, and 4) tool_call fencing tokens to anchor tool call boundaries. Streaming stability: add a SnapshotMarker token sequence that the stream injector emits at safe checkpoints and a deterministic resume flow that replays minimal context to regenerate the KV cache when a reconnection happens. Tool/function calling: add explicit fencing metadata so functions invoked by adapters are only executed after a complete tool_call block has been received; partial tool payloads now surface as structured warnings rather than immediate failures. Validation and errors: implement human-readable validation errors mapped to an actionable error taxonomy (error_code, user_hint, recovery_hint) surfaced in the API and in the OpenAI-compat shim. The runtime will emit structured error frames on the stream (with an escape token) allowing clients to handle retries or fallbacks without breaking streaming parsers. OpenAI compatibility layer: add a translator that maps common function_call shapes to the new schema-handshake and back to legacy function_call when necessary; this preserves existing SDK behaviour while enabling the new validation features. Backwards compatibility: default behaviour remains unchanged; customers must set response_format or an adapter flag to enable adaptive_strictness and snapshotting. Tests and telemetry: add unit tests for handshake negotiation, fuzz tests for interleaved tool calls, and metrics (handshake_success, resume_rate, schema_violation_rate). Docs: update API reference, add a migration guide for SDK authors and a troubleshooting page with common error scenarios and recommended remediation steps. Implementation notes: no on-disk migration required; changes are mostly runtime/kafka message schema and small SDK adapters. Rollout: feature gated behind feature flag response_format_v3 and controlled rollout for Dedicated accounts for 2 weeks before global flip. Related: builds on previous schema work but intentionally exposes a smaller, developer-friendly surface for early adopter feedback.

review_comments: Sasha Nguyen: Requested that the handshake include an explicit backward-compatibility flag so older SDKs can decide whether to attempt translation. Also asked for more integration tests around function_call edge cases.
Author (Amira Patel): Added a backward_compat flag and expanded the translator to stub legacy function_call shapes when requested. Added two integration tests to cover partial payload interleaving.
Diego Ramos: Noted a potential race in resume_manager when multiple reconnects happen concurrently; suggested deferring resume attempts via a single-run worker per session_id.
Author (Amira Patel): Implemented single-run worker and added a comment with reasoning; added a unit test for concurrent reconnects.
Luca Moretti: Approved after addressing race and after CI green. Observability notes: please expose handshake_success and resume_rate at 1m granularity.
CI Bot: One flaky test (resume_fuzz_test) failed on first run; reran and passed. All checks green.
release_notes: Introduce opt-in response_format v3 handshake: adaptive strictness levels, snapshot markers for stream resume, tool_call fencing, and human-readable validation errors. Backwards compatible by default; feature-flagged rollout. Includes SDK adapters and migration guide.
